subject: Operational indemnity & buyout schedule tied to uptime bands
messages:
From: Elaine Johnson <elaine.johnson@medsyshealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medsyshealth.com, gavin.lee@medsyshealth.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational indemnity / buyout schedule proposal for uptime and latency breaches

Ben —

Thanks for the productive call yesterday. MedSys legal and procurement have reviewed the SLA language and we need to close the following commercial asks before legal can sign:

1) Convert recurring service credits into a limited cash buyout when repeat P1/P2 events occur. Specifically: if we experience >= 3 P1-class latency incidents (>= 50% traffic impacted, > 5 minutes) within a rolling 90-day window, we want the option to trigger a cash buyout equal to 30% of monthly committed fees for that month, escalating to 60% if events continue for two consecutive months.

2) A 60-day termination right with pro-rated refund if the weekly availability over a rolling 30-day window falls below 99.5% for three consecutive weeks.

3) A non-cumulative operational indemnity pool ("fee-at-risk pool") of $150k held in escrow for the first 12 months. This pool converts to liquidated damages if events described in (1) occur and are not cured in the 60-day cure window.

We appreciate Redwood's position on unlimited liability, so we're trying to be surgical: this model converts operational credit remedies into a predictable cash recourse tied to measurable operational thresholds, and gives MedSys a clear exit if reliability materially degrades.

I've attached the redline our counsel prepared (medsys_redlines_30Jul.pdf) and highlighted where we believe the buyout conversion must be explicit. Gavin included a short list of monitoring anchors (service-dashboard links) in the appendix.

Please confirm receipt and let us know which points Redwood cannot accept so we can prioritize.

- Elaine
Elaine Johnson
Head of Procurement, MedSys Health
elaine.johnson@medsyshealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Johnson <elaine.johnson@medsyshealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational indemnity / buyout schedule proposal for uptime and latency breaches

Elaine — thanks, received and reviewed the redlines. Appreciate the clarity and the way you tied remedies to concrete thresholds. A few quick points from our side up front:

- We understand the need for convertible remedies, but unlimited or uncapped cash conversion creates material risk for Redwood given third-party infra and burst events. We can work to a capped fee-at-risk construct with clear triggers, observability hooks, and an agreed cure timetable.

- The 60-day termination right on a rolling 30-day availability window is aggressive. We can offer a staged termination path: a 90-day remediation/cure period with predefined remediation milestones and an optional 60-day exit only if remediation milestones are missed by >2 weeks.

- Escrow mechanics: we prefer a deposit-based holdback (Redwood posts a cash holdback or letter of credit sized to the pool) rather than third-party escrow to avoid distribution delays, but we are open to a neutral escrow agent with pre-defined disbursement rules.

I'm looping in Aditya (legal) and Marissa (AE) to draft a counterproposal that preserves MedSys's protection while limiting open-ended exposures for Redwood. Attached is our initial framing (redwood_counter_proposal_20270731.pdf) — it includes: capped buyout pool at $150k, a 2-tier availability band, conversion rules for repeated P1s, and a 90-day staged remediation path.

Can we book 30 minutes next week to walk the models with Gavin and your procurement counsel?

Best,

Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0198

From: Elaine Johnson <elaine.johnson@medsyshealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medsyshealth.com, gavin.lee@medsyshealth.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational indemnity / buyout schedule proposal for uptime and latency breaches

Ben —

Thanks for the quick reply and for the draft. A few clarifications from MedSys legal after reviewing Redwood's framing:

- The buyout cap ($150k) is acceptable as a maximum, but we need a mechanism that allows for partial conversion earlier in the incident sequence (e.g., a first conversion of 15% after the 3rd P1 in the 90 days, increment to 30% after a 4th P1). That gives us more immediate recourse.

- We can be flexible on the remediation timeline if Redwood commits to specific operational milestones and a public postmortem cadence. Our priority is a deterministic clock and verifiable telemetry anchors (we listed the dashboard endpoints in the redline).

- Regarding escrow vs. holdback: MedSys prefers neutral escrow administered by a named agent (we proposed IronTrust Escrow) to avoid perceived conflicts of interest.

I've attached a short note from our counsel that marks the conversion schedule we'd accept if Redwood can commit to the remediation milestone plan.

Would Thursday 8/5 10:00 PT work for a joint session? Gavin can share the telemetry views and we can go line-by-line on the conversion rules.

Regards,
Elaine

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Johnson <elaine.johnson@medsyshealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational indemnity / buyout schedule proposal for uptime and latency breaches

Elaine — thanks, Thursday 8/5 10:00 PT works for our side. Quick summary of Redwood's closing posture so the meeting can be productive:

1) Fee-at-risk pool: Redwood accepts a $150k capped pool held via a neutral escrow agent (we will propose escrow agreement language ahead of the call).

2) Conversion schedule compromise: partial conversion allowed after the 3rd P1 (15% of monthly commit), then 30% after a 4th P1 in the 90-day window, with a hard cap of 60% for sustained events. We will add an explicit rule that conversions are non-cumulative across different calendar months (to avoid double-counting).

3) Remediation and termination: Redwood agrees to a staged remediation path with explicit milestones and a 90-day primary cure window. MedSys will be able to exercise a 60-day termination if Redwood misses two consecutive milestone checkpoints by >14 days.

4) Monitoring anchors: Redwood will publish a signed monitoring SLA (endpoints and metrics) and provide a read-only dashboard view for MedSys. Any dispute about triggering telemetry will be escalated to the neutral escrow agent whose rules will govern disbursement timing.

Next steps: Aditya will circulate a redline to the escrow agreement and conversion schedule by EOD Wednesday. Marissa will set the 8/5 meeting and include an agenda that allocates 15 minutes to telemetry anchors, 15 minutes to conversion rules, and 15 minutes to escrow mechanics. I will also include a draft DocuSign link for execution readiness after the meeting.

If you want to circulate the counsel note before the meeting, that will help us move faster.

Best,
Ben
